COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Binary Arithmetic Operations, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Binary Arithmetic Operations.

2. When learning Network Security, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Network Security.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Network Security.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Network Security.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Security.

3. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Remove all guards
   B. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   C. Run with the tool
   D. Work alone with eyes closed

4. When learning Web Development Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Web Development Fundamentals.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Web Development Fundamentals.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Web Development Fundamentals.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Web Development Fundamentals.

5. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Ignore burnt cables
   B. Overload every socket
   C. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   D. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun

6. When learning Object Oriented Programming Implementation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.

7. When learning Relational Database Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Relational Database Fundamentals.

8. When learning Logic Circuits, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Logic Circuits.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Circuits.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Logic Circuits.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Logic Circuits.

9. When learning Data Representation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Data Representation.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Representation.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Representation.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Representation.

10. When learning Structured Query Language, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Structured Query Language.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Structured Query Language.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Structured Query Language.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Structured Query Language.

11. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Input Cable Tester
   B. Information and Communication Technology
   C. Internal Cooking Timer
   D. International Cricket Team

12. When learning Computer Network Standards and Protocols, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.

13. When learning Object Oriented Programming Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.

14. When learning Logic Gates, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Logic Gates.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Logic Gates.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Logic Gates.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Gates.

15. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. CPU
   B. Keyboard
   C. Monitor
   D. Speaker

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Logic Circuits and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Computer Network Standards and Protocols and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
